title: Chocolate pots de crème
summary: Small, dense chocolate custards baked in a water bath; richer and smoother than a mousse.
steps: Heat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F). Set six small ramekins or pots in a roasting tin.
Heat the cream and almond milk until steaming, pour over the chocolate and leave 2 minutes, then stir until smooth.
Whisk the yolks, erythritol, vanilla, salt and espresso powder. Slowly whisk in the chocolate cream and strain into a jug.
Pour into the pots and add hot water to the tin to come halfway up. Cover the tin loosely with foil.
Bake 30–35 minutes, until set at the edge with a slight wobble in the centre. Cool, then refrigerate at least 4 hours.
dairy_free_notes: Coconut cream makes an equally dense custard; the chocolate covers most of the coconut flavour.
tips: Unsweetened chocolate keeps the carbs low; taste the warm chocolate cream and add a few drops of stevia if you like it sweeter.

origin.history: Pots de crème are named for the small lidded cups they were baked and served in. French porcelain makers were producing sets of these custard cups by the 1700s, a sign of how fashionable the little custards were at table. Vanilla, coffee and chocolate are the classic flavours.
